column2: Curriculum Outline: Pilot Project using Avatars
Session 1
column3: Theme: Introduction at Avatar's house

column2: Basic Flow
column3: Student Participation

column2: Avatar Introduces himself (3 features)
column3: Students Introduce themselves

column2: Avatar talks about things he likes to do in his free time
column3: Students share their interests, educator asks to find common likes and dislikes
column4: Positive Peer Interaction + Finding common interests

column2: Avatar introduces his family + what he likes to do with them
column3:
Students participate in the discussion: Raise your hand if:
- How many of you have siblings
- How many of you have older/younger siblings
- How many of you have a pet

column2: Ice breakers activity depending on learners
column3: Dance Off/ Sing Along/Other Interactive game
column4: Identifying baseline- Recognition of emotions, building a rapport

column2: Session 2
column3: Theme: Avatar goes to a birthday party

column2: Basic Flow
column3: Student Participation

column2: Avatar is excited to meet his friends A, B, C
column3: Identify 2 or 3 of their friends: How do they know each each other, what do you like doing together?
column4: Create Baseline for Rules of Interaction with social circle

column2: Avatar seeks help in choosing a present
column3: Identifying interests, likes and matching it with a relevant gift

column2: Avatar seeks help in making a birthday card
column3: How can we express our feelings towards our friends?

column2: Avatar goes to the birthday party
column3: Greeting people at the party
column4: Rules of interaction with social circle

column3: Which activity should the avatar participate in? How does he feel included?
column4: Meaningful Communication + Positive Peer interaction + Finding common interests

column2: Avatar consoles a friend who is feeling bad for being left out
column3: Discuss: How can we console people when they are upset?
column4: Dealing with a negative emotion: sadness, meaningful conversation

column2: Session 3
column3: Theme: Avatar goes to a Grocery Store

column2: Basic Flow
column3: Student Participation

column2: Avatar is Overwhelmed/Scared to go to the supermarket
column3: Discuss: How can we be better prepared for situations like shopping?
column4: Identifying negative feeling, dealing with a negative emotion: anxiety

column2: Avatar works on a list
column3: Students participate by working on lists provided to them

column2: Avatar prepares to go to the store
column3: Students discuss what all we need before we go: Shopping bag, masks, etc

column2: Avatar at the shop needs help with finding items
column3:
Students help with: Finding the right aisle 
- Checking Quantity, Price
- Finding a substitute

column2: Avatar asks for help
column3: Discuss: How should we speak with the Supermarket staff

column2: Billing
column3: Students discuss payment modes, getting the right change, receiving a bill
column4: Rules of interaction at a grocery store + Money concepts

column2: Avatar meets elderly neighbourhood lady
column3: Discuss: How can we interact with our neighbour? Can we offer help?
column4: Rules of interaction with social circle

column2: Getting home safely
Session 4
column3: Theme: Avatar goes to the Doctor

column2: Basic Flow
column3: Student Participation

column2: Avatar is experiencing discomfort- "I'm not feeling well"
column3:
Practice with students: How to ask questions? 
- What happened Kikof?
- Where is it hurting you?
- How did you get sick?
column4: Dealing with a negative emotion: pain + meaningful conversation

column2: Avatar explains his stomach is hurting and he is not able to stand or do his homework
column3:
Practice with students: Helping someone who is sick
- Get some rest! Maybe you should lie down
- Do you want to take some medicine? 
- Is it hurting a lot? Maybe we should go to a doctor
column4: Essential Life skills + Meaningful conversation + Planning (Cognitive Functioning)

column2: Avatar tries to rest but isn't feeling good at all
column3:
Practice with students: Helping someone who is sick
- Calling Parent
- Suggest going to a doctor

column2: Avatar wishes to make an appointment with a doctor
column3:
Practice with students: Making an appointment 
- Identifying a clinic
- Make an appointment for an emergency 
- Checking if we can make it in time for the appointment: Give two options available

column2: Avatar goes to the clinic
column3:
Practice with students: What happens at the clinic 
- Reception, Waiting area, Interaction with Nurse, Doctor
column4: Essential Life skills + Meaningful conversation + Planning (Cognitive Functioning)

column2: Avatar wishes to buy medicinces
column3:
Practice with the students: Purchasing medicines 
- Concept of a pharmacy, prescription
- Billing

column2: Avatar comes back home, brother is having a burger
column3: Practice with students: Getting Rest + Staying Healthy

column2: Avatar goes to his room to rest
column3:
What can we say to kikof because he is sick? 
- Get well soon?
- How can i help you?

column2: Avatar wakes up from a nightmare
column3: How can we console someone who is scared?

column2: Session 5
column3: Theme: Avatar gets lost in a park

column2: Basic Flow
column3: Student Participation

column2: Avatar decides what to do this Weekend
column3: What goes into making a decision? : Weather Conditions, what we feel like doing

column2: Avatar is excited for his walk in the park
column3: What goes into making a decision? : Weather Conditions, what we feel like doing

column2: A boy approaches the avatar for a conversation, he has a bag + map (identifying a tourist)
column3: Practice with students: How can the avatar help the tourist find his way?
column4: Create Baseline for Rules of Interaction with social circle

column2: Avatar wishes to get an ice cream, two stalls: one is crowded, one doesn't have any of his favourite flavours. Avatar is frustrated
column3:
Practice with students: How can avatar feel calm in this situation? 
- How can the avatar make a decision in this case?
column4: Planning- Cognitive Skills + Dealing with a negative emotion: Frustration

column2: Avatar realises he is lost
column3: Practice with students: How can he keep calm?
column4: Dealing with a negative emotion: panic

column2: Avatar encounters a stranger, who offers to help
column3:
Practice with students: Should the avatar seek help from strangers?
Should the avatar try to find a police officer
column4: Essential Life skills + Meaningful conversation + Rules of interaction with a stranger

column2: Avatar interacts with traffic police officer
column3:
Practice with students: What all information should we tell the officer? 
- Contacting your parent/guardian
column4: Essential Life skills + Meaningful conversation + Planning (Cognitive Functioning)

column2: Avatar is able to safely go home and relax
column3: Fun activity with students to unwind
